detail: The preparing half of drawing runs on its own thread, so busy scenes (3,000 to 4,000 draws a frame) cost less on a slower processor. With the CPU held at its base clock the title demo ran at 28.3 against 26.8 frames per second (about 29.5 with the per-draw cuts of #187); no difference at full speed
note: PIPE=0 turns it off; the settings window's “Two-thread drawing” box; on by default since #186; online play with different settings is not tested

feature: Frames shown without waiting for the monitor
detail: The port paces itself at 30 frames per second on its own clock and no longer waits for the monitor's vblank as a second clock. On a 60 Hz monitor a frame that took 33 to 50 ms no longer waits for 50 ms, so 30 does not fall to 20
note: D3D12_VSYNC=1 waits for the vblank again, D3D12_VSYNC=0 allows tearing; #185; not tried on a real 60 Hz monitor (a test switch stood in for it)

detail: A 2 Players frame no longer needs two batches with a GPU wait between them, and draws that used few vertices of a big mesh copy only those vertices. A 2 vs 2 on one stage: about 18-24 frames per second before, about 28-30 after, with two-thread drawing on; 1 Player is unchanged
